question: What are Canada's mandatory sustainability disclosure requirements for listed companies?

passages.title: Global Sustainability Reporting Briefing
passages.section: 4. Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and ESRS
passages.text: 4. Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and ESRS. The EU's mandatory sustainability reporting law and its technical standards. Components: Double materiality (impacts on people and planet, plus financial risk); 2 cross-cutting and 10 topical ESRS; mandatory limited assurance; digital tagging, now postponed. Revised ESRS adopted on 3 July 2026 cut mandatory datapoints by over 60% and total datapoints by over 70% (European Commission). In scope: EU companies with more than 1,000 employees and more than EUR 450m net turnover. Non-EU groups are in scope with over EUR 450m EU turnover and an EU subsidiary or branch above EUR 200m (Latham & Watkins). Suppliers under 1,000 employees can decline data requests beyond a voluntary SME standard. Enforcement: Penalties set by each Member State; statutory auditors or accredited assurers sign off; national market regulators supervise listed issuers.
passages.location: p.2, "4. Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and ESRS"

passages.title: Global Sustainability Reporting Briefing
passages.text: 7. Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD). A conduct obligation, not only a disclosure one. Components: Identify, prevent and remediate adverse human rights and environmental impacts in the company's own operations and chain of activities, with a risk-based focus. In scope: EU companies with more than 5,000 employees and EUR 1.5bn net worldwide turnover, and non-EU companies with EUR 1.5bn EU turnover. Compliance is required from 26 July 2029 (Morrison Foerster). Enforcement: National supervisory authorities with administrative fines; the Omnibus narrowed the liability and penalty provisions (Accountancy Europe).
passages.location: p.3, "7. Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD)"

passages.title: Global Sustainability Reporting Briefing
passages.section: 10. Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) and BRSR Core
passages.text: 10. Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) and BRSR Core. India's mandatory ESG report, set by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Components: Full BRSR covers the nine principles of India's National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct, from environment to employee welfare to consumer fairness. BRSR Core is a subset of nine attributes (including GHG emissions, water, energy, waste, gender diversity and workforce safety) that must be independently assessed or assured. In scope: The top 1,000 listed companies by market capitalization file the full BRSR. BRSR Core assessment or assurance extends to all 1,000 from FY 2026-27. Value chain disclosures for the top 250 are voluntary from FY 2025-26 after SEBI's March 2025 deferral (Sustainability 101). Enforcement: A listing obligation under SEBI's LODR Regulation 34(2)(f), filed with the annual report; SEBI and the stock exchanges can impose fines and other actions for non-compliance or misstatement.
passages.location: pp.4-5, "10. Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) and BRSR Core"

passages.title: ESG Frameworks Comparison
passages.text: Framework/Standard: CSRD. Full Name: Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive. Focus: Comprehensive sustainability reporting. Scope: EU companies and non-EU companies operating in the EU. Reporting Requirement: Mandatory for large EU companies, phased approach starting in 2024. Alignment with Other Standards: Aligned with European Green Deal, GRI. Industry-Specific Guidance: No, but includes sector-specific indicators. Key Features: Expands on NFRD, integrates double materiality (financial + sustainability impact)

passages.title: Novata ESG Standards and Frameworks Guide
passages.text: The International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability Disclosure Standards, developed by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), are designed to help investors and capital markets assess and disclose sustainability-related risks and opportunities. Its first two standards—IFRS S1 (general sustainability-related financial disclosures) and IFRS S2 (climate-related disclosures)—were published in 2023 and are now seeing rapid regulatory uptake, with over 36 jurisdictions committed to aligning with them.
